title: A 600-Year-Old Ming Palace in Nanjing Is Now a Street Market | China Travel Expert
description:
POV: you're walking through Nanjing's Chaotian Palace (朝天宫) — a Ming imperial complex about 600 years old that today hosts a weekend street fair under its eaves.

The site was renamed Chaotian Palace in 1384, under the founding Ming (Hongwu) emperor. 'Chaotian' means 'facing Heaven / the emperor' — this was where officials and their children rehearsed the etiquette of having an audience with the emperor before grand ceremonies. The halls you see today were largely rebuilt in the 1860s (Qing), and the complex is now the Nanjing Municipal Museum — one of Jiangnan's best-preserved groups of Ming-and-Qing-style official architecture.

Expert Tip: go on a fair day and you'll find stalls lined up right under the red pillars and glazed eaves — then step into the museum halls behind them; the contrast is the whole point.

南京朝天宫：1384年明太祖时定名「朝天宫」，是明代官员演习朝见天子礼仪的地方；现存建筑多为1860年代重建，如今是南京市博物馆。600年的宫殿和玻璃商场，你更想逛哪个？
